top.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
top.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

According to SPORT , the Catalan club is assessing different profiles in order to improve their defensive stability for the second half of the season. However, the club’s financial restrictions and the contractual situations of their preferred targets could make the recruitment process particularly complicated ahead of the January 2027 transfer window. Barcelona’s defensive recruitment a priority for Deco Barcelona have made considerable progress in rebuilding their squad, with Deco’s recruitment work and La Masia’s contribution helping the club develop a stronger group of players. However, central defence remains an area where the sporting department believes further investment is necessary, something that Deco agreed to recently . Given the injuries Barcelona have suffered this season, Flick needs defenders who can operate comfortably in a high defensive line, contribute to building attacks from the back and cope with the space left behind when Barcelona commit players forward. Deco and Flick are not in favour of signing Lisandro Martinez. Was it one of the best bouts of the year or a sloppy bar brawl? Should Gane have lost a point for the eye poke that the referee initially missed? top.title: Golden boy back! Vincent Kompany backs Jamal Musiala to prove Bayern chiefs wrong after health and contract storm
top.description: FC Bayern München v FK Bodo/Glimt - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 - Getty Images Sport Jamal Musiala is set to return to the Bayern Munich squad for Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln after two months on the sidelines. Amid intense scrutiny from club chiefs over his fitness and lucrative contract, head coach Vincent Kompany has fiercely praised the playmaker's resilience. Musiala ready for long-awaited squad return Jamal Musiala is poised to return to the Bayern Munich matchday squad for Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln following nearly two months out of action. Head coach Vincent Kompany confirmed on Thursday that the Germany international has recovered from a thigh muscle fibre tear sustained during international warm-ups in late September . "The way Jamal fights and what he's showing right now - I hope you'll all get to see more of it over the coming months and that he can demonstrate it on the pitch," Kompany said. "He's showing an incredible mentality and a real hunger. He'll probably be in the squad tomorrow." Standing firm amid boardroom scrutiny Musiala's return arrives during a turbulent period off the pitch, with honorary president Uli Hoeness recently questioning whether the 23-year-old can justify his reported €25 million annual salary following repeated health setbacks. Having also suffered neurological absence seizures during pre-season in August, Musiala has managed just four appearances so far in the 2026-27 campaign. Kompany, however, backed his star to emerge stronger from the ordeal, pointing to Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane as proof of what players can achieve in Munich. "When players like him go through a difficult spell, they can draw strength from it - both mentally and physically," Kompany stated. "When I arrived, he was a 'golden child'. Seeing how he's handling the whole situation now is something special. I hope that in six months' time, it'll be a completely different story." Positive updates on Luis Diaz and Alphonso Davies Alongside Musiala's impending comeback, Kompany delivered encouraging fitness bulletins regarding wingers Luis Diaz and full-back Alphonso Davies. While Friday's visit from Koln comes slightly too soon for Diaz, the Colombian international is nearing full availability. "Lucho is doing very well. He's had a good week. Tomorrow's still a bit too soon for him, but we'll be able to get him back in action within the next seven days," Kompany revealed, before adding a brief reassurance on Davies: "Phonzy will be fine; I can't say any more than that at the moment." Reinforcements arrive for crucial winter run Getting key stars back on the grass provides a timely boost for Kompany, who has also just returned from his own four-week medical absence. With Bayern sitting atop the Bundesliga as the only unbeaten team across Europe's top five leagues, Musiala's creativity will prove vital across eight fixtures before the winter break.

top.title: Andriy Shevchenko hits back at Mykhailo Mudryk as Ukraine legend makes 'baseless slander' claim over doping ban controversy
top.description: Andriy Shevchenko - Getty Images Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko has reacted furiously to allegations made by Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk regarding a failed drugs test that stalled the winger’s career. The former AC Milan and Chelsea striker, now leading the Ukrainian Association of Football, has dismissed the claims as a "baseless slander" against the national federation. Row erupts over Mudryk's meldonium suspension The dispute stems from a positive test for meldonium that sidelined the 25-year-old Chelsea loanee from November 2024 until July 2026 . Although Mudryk initially received a four-year ban, the sanction was lifted after he accepted breaching anti-doping rules. Speaking on the YouTube channel Guest of Gordon , Mudryk blamed the national setup for his failed test , accused the UAF of leaking case details and delaying his return, and claimed Shevchenko offered little support. In response, the UAF president alleged that Mudryk's representatives had repeatedly asked the federation to find an employee to take the blame. Mudryk points the finger as Shevchenko hits back Addressing the saga, Mudryk insisted the banned substance could only have entered his system in Ukraine. "The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team," he said. "It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now. I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England." He added that it "points to the fact it was in a national team camp", replying bluntly when asked if he blamed the national side: "Yes, exactly." Shevchenko swiftly rejected those allegations. "I want to express my position regarding Mykhailo Mudryk's accusations," he said. "Loud statements were made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally." Addressing the alleged push for a scapegoat, Shevchenko stressed that official inquiries cleared the federation. "Such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work," he said. "The accusations made by Mykhailo's representatives were not confirmed or substantiated by evidence after numerous investigations and checks. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English FA confirm this." It started with a suspected power unit issue, with Verstappen reporting a lack of power on his out-lap. top.title: Thomas Frank shares his feelings on Crystal Palace appointment
top.description: Thomas Frank shares his feelings on Crystal Palace appointment Thomas Frank Returns to Crystal Palace as Relegation Fight Begins Thomas Frank is back, and he sounds exactly like a man who has had enough time away to think clearly. Crystal Palace have appointed the 53-year-old on a two-and-a-half-year deal, and his first message was simple. He is refreshed, reflective and ready for another go in the Premier League. Palace need that. They are bottom of the table, short on momentum and heading into a survival battle that will demand clarity more than noise. Frank arrives after a bruising end to his previous spell at Tottenham, where he was dismissed in February, less than eight months after taking charge. He could have stayed away longer. He chose not to. Thomas Frank Embraces Palace Challenge There was no attempt to dress it up. Frank admitted the break had been enjoyable. He travelled to Japan and Australia, spent time in Denmark and relaxed with family and friends. As he put it, he had been “visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine”. Photo IMAGO He had every reason to extend that time off too. “I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time,” he said. Then came the line that tells you where his head is now, “I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.” Still, Palace convinced him. The club’s internal pitch clearly mattered. Frank singled out chairman Steve Parish, along with Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody, as key figures in persuading him this was the right job at the right time. Crystal Palace Need Fast Impact That matters because sentiment gets you nowhere at the bottom of the Premier League. Palace need points, quickly. Frank’s reign starts with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday, and there is no gentle easing-in period. The task is obvious, steady the team, sharpen the structure and lift belief. Frank also made it clear that his time out of football was not spent feeling sorry for himself. “If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better,” said Frank. “Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. top.title: Liverpool receive Alex Scott update ahead of January window
top.description: Liverpool receive Alex Scott update ahead of January window Alex Scott Transfer Latest as Liverpool Track Bournemouth Midfielder Alex Scott is moving back into focus, for Bournemouth and for clubs circling around him. Chelsea tried in the summer and are expected to come again in January. Arsenal remain interested. Liverpool do too, and that part matters given who is now at Anfield. Scott has 18 months left on his Bournemouth deal. That changes the conversation. It does not force a sale, but it does sharpen the decision making. Renew him, sell him, or risk watching leverage slip away. That is where Bournemouth are. Liverpool Interest Makes Sense Liverpool want midfield depth and they want quality on the ball. Scott fits that brief. He is technically clean, sees passes early and plays with control. He also knows what Andoni Iraola wants. Scott was an important part of the coach’s setup at Bournemouth before Iraola left for Liverpool, so there is no mystery here about suitability. That does not mean a transfer is close. It means the logic is obvious. Liverpool know the player, the player knows the method, and the contract situation keeps this alive. Marco Rose Addresses Bournemouth Situation Marco Rose was direct when asked about the noise. “We talk everyday about football and about personal stuff. We have a good connection and we know how it works in this business. “Bournemouth is a top club for young players to improve. He is quite committed with the club and we can’t change the rumours. He is a Bournemouth player and he likes to be a Bournemouth player. The other things are not of interest to me as a coach.” That is what managers say when they want calm and would rather discuss availability than transfer chatter. Alex Scott Injury Return Comes at Good Time For now, the immediate issue is football. Scott is back after a hamstring problem that kept him out of four Premier League games. Rose confirmed he is ready to start, saying: “We have many games in the upcoming weeks, even next week three games, so a lot of choices and for sure he’s going to start in one of those games. “We have to increase his match time step by step. But he had a good two weeks with training and some rest and now I think Alex is ready, Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start.” After missing eight matches with a thigh injury, he returned to the squad for Bournemouth’s 2-1 win at Ipswich before the international break. The transfer talk can wait. His football cannot.

top.title: 'It was certainly a shock' - Vincent Kompany reveals honest truth behind four-week Bayern Munich absence
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-BAYERN MUNICH-ARSENAL - AFP Vincent Kompany is officially back on the touchline for Bayern Munich ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln. After spending four weeks away recovering from a health scare, the Belgian coach has opened up on his medical tests, rival managers' support, and watching his side from home. Kompany returns to the Allianz Arena dugout Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is back on the touchline ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln at the Allianz Arena. Having missed four weeks following a health scare caused by meningeal irritation, the 40-year-old welcomed his international players back to Sabener Strasse on Thursday after receiving full medical clearance . "I'm very grateful for the support I've received from the club and the doctors. I'm feeling really well again now and am delighted to be back with the team," Kompany said. "All the tests came back positive. I have to say, I'm in very good health; we've done lots of tests, all of which have come back clear." Admitting he ignored warning signs Kompany admitted his enforced break served as a wake-up call after he initially failed to listen to his body following an earlier Champions League tie against Arsenal. Despite the initial alarm, he thanked rival managers and his family for standing by him during his recovery. "I don't want to play it down; it was certainly a shock. But it was a result of me carrying on when I really should have taken a break," Kompany explained. "As well as my family, I'd also like to thank the coaching community. We're always competing against one another, but almost every coach has got in touch with me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps even had our differences." Praising his backroom staff from afar During his time away, Kompany stepped back completely from matchday decisions, trusting assistants Rene Maric, Aaron Danks, Floribert Ngalula and Daniel Fradley to maintain standards. Watching from home, he highlighted Bayern's fearless Champions League display against Atletico Madrid as a standout memory. "I didn't make any decisions," he noted. "When the head coach is absent, the handover has to be such that things carry on as they always do. They managed that very well. I really enjoyed the Atletico match. It was one of the finest moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn't there." Motivated for the pre-Christmas sprint Refreshed and armed with fresh tactical ideas gathered during his time off, Kompany is eager to lead Europe's last remaining unbeaten side in the top five leagues into a gruelling run of eight matches in 29 days. "There's one person at FC Bayern who is really motivated for this game against Koln. I've been waiting for four weeks," Kompany concluded. "If the players can sense my motivation, we'll have a good foundation for tomorrow's match."

top.title: UFC Qatar weigh-in results: Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling official, 1 fighter misses weight
top.description: Tahir Abdullayev was the lone UFC Qatar fighter to miss weight | Ed Mulholland, Zuffa LLC The UFC Qatar official weigh-ins were mostly without drama, especially with the main card set, but preliminary fighter Tahir Abdullayev spoiled what could have been a perfect session. Ahead of Saturday’s event at Ali Bin Hamad al-Attiyah Arena in Doha, Qatar, 24 fighters stepped to the scale and Abdullayev was the lone miss Friday morning. Abdullayev weighed in at 172 pounds, one pound over the limit for a non-title welterweight bout, while his opponent Jake Matthews weighed in at 170 pounds. The UFC later announced that Abdullayev vs. Matthews will proceed at a catchweight, with Abdullayev forfeiting 20 percent of his purse as penalty. Fortunately for fans, headliners Jiri Prochazka and Navajo Stirling weighed in without a hitch, with both fighters making a statement by registering at the championship limit of 205 pounds. Co-main event featherweights Aljamain Sterling and Kevin Vallejos also hit championship weight at 145 pounds on the dot. Also of note, two-time featherweight title challenger Brian Ortega successfully made weight as he moves up a division, coming in at 155.5 pounds. His opponent, veteran lightweight Dan Hooker, weighed in at 156 pounds. Check out UFC Qatar official weigh-in results below. top.title: 'We have a strong squad' - Harry Kane issues Champions League battle cry as Bayern Munich target ultimate European glory
top.description: Atletico de Madrid v FC Bayern München - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Harry Kane has sent a defiant message to the rest of European football, insisting that Bayern Munich possess all the necessary tools to reclaim the Champions League trophy. The England captain believes the Bavarian giants are ready to end their wait for continental success following a heart-breaking exit in the competition last term. European silverware remains the primary objective The pursuit of the UEFA Champions League title has become the defining mission for Kane and his Bayern teammates. After several years without touching the most prestigious trophy in club football, the English striker has publicly voiced the collective ambition of the German giants to return to the summit of the European game. For a club with the stature of the Rekordmeister, a six-year hiatus from winning the competition is viewed as far too long. Reflecting on the current state of the squad, Kane expressed immense confidence in the personnel assembled at the Allianz Arena. The forward is adamant that the blend of experience and talent within the dressing room makes them a match for anyone on the continent. "The Champions League is a major objective for me and for the team. We have a strong squad, made up of incredible players," Kane said in an interview with French news outlet Foot Mercato . Learning from the pain of Paris The memories of last season's exit remain fresh in the mind of the 33-year-old. Bayern reached the semi-finals of the 2025-26 campaign, only to be narrowly edged out by Paris Saint-Germain in a high-scoring 6-5 aggregate defeat. Despite the disappointment of falling just short of the final, Kane maintains a level of respect for the opponents who ended their run, as reported by Bulinews. "Last season, the matches against PSG were crazy, it was incredibly close, and being knocked out by the team that won the title twice in a row was nothing to be ashamed of," Kane remarked while looking back at that continental thriller. The striker believes that those high-pressure encounters have provided the squad with invaluable experience that will serve them well as they navigate the knockout rounds this time around. Rather than lingering on the loss, the team is using it as fuel for their current European charge. With Vincent Kompany now entering his third season at the Allianz Arena, the Belgian tactician's footballing identity has become deeply hardwired into the squad. top.title: Ducks "flat as a pancake" in shutout loss in Colorado
top.description: Nov 19, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Colorado Avalanche center Brock Nelson (11) celebrates after his goal in the second period against the Anaheim Ducks at Ball Arena. DENVER – Joel Quenneville provided the most aptly succinct description of the Anaheim Ducks first shutout loss of the season. “We were flat as a pancake,” the Ducks coach said. Anaheim’s chronic defensive issues persisted following a competitive opening period, and the Ducks previously scalding hot offense was completely snowed under by the Colorado Avalanche in a sound defeat, 4-0, on Thursday at Ball Arena. Anaheim (11-11-1, 23 points) has lost four of its last five games following a five-game winning streak and has allowed four or more goals in 14 of its 23 games. “I think everything (was disconnected),” Jackson LaCombe said. “We turned too many pucks over. Just didn't have any jam on the offense. Throwing pucks away early. Didn't have any possession time. There’s things we’ve gotta fix.” Cutter Gauthier’s historically prolific 10-game goal streak came to a halt. Gauthier recorded just two shots and only one on the power play, as the Avalanche penalty kill rightly shaded his one-timer spot. Teemu Selanne maintains his hold on the longest goal streak in franchise history (11 games, 1997-98). All of Anaheim’s top performers were stagnant against Colorado, with Gauthier, Leo Carlsson, Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund combining for three total shots. The Ducks spent an inordinate amount of time in their own defensive zone, as they again turned the puck over on their half of the ice, struggled on clears and couldn’t connect on clean breakouts. Stian Solberg, 2024 first-round pick, made his NHL debut, and with the 20-year-old Norwegian defenseman cracking the line-up, Anaheim iced a blue line with an average age of 22.67 years old. “Tough loss, but most fun game I ever played,” Solberg said. “It's cool to be out there on the biggest stage in the world. It's just something we've been kind of just looking at your whole life and when it finally happens, it's very special.” Nicolas Roy opened the scoring after an all-around failure by Anaheim on the opening draw of the second period. Beckett Sennecke couldn’t control the puck, fell at his own blue line, and the Avalanche pounced to send Roy walking around Lukáš Dostál, 1-0, eight seconds into the middle frame. Momentum continued to slide Colorado’s way, as Brock Nelson blasted a power-play one-timer three minutes later, 2-0. The Avalanche had the first three power plays of the night. Nelson netted another just under seven minutes later, as he toe-dragged around Jackson LaCombe and picked top glove on Dostál, 3-0. Another turnover ended up in the back of the Ducks net, as Devon Toews finished in the slot, 4-0, with just under 10 minutes to play. top.title: Cowboys Could See Return of Injured Breakout Playmaker
top.description: Tyler Goodson #32 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty The Dallas Cowboys have delved into a good deal of drama this week, which is not where any NFL team wants its season to be after 10 weeks. But the Cowboys made their move with the demotion of defensive coordinator Christian Parker, following the 46-40 loss to the 49ers last Sunday, in which the team gave up 584 yards of offense and three plays that went for 66 yards on their own. Dallas made selling out to get to the quarterback a priority and while there was some success in that, the 49ers burned them enough times to make the whole enterprise of the Cowboys’ defense look futile. The issue has dominated news from The Star since, even as other issues have continues to crop up. One of them is backup running back Tyler Goodson. No doubt, Goodson had been one of the positive additions to the roster–one of the few–this season, signed to be the backup running back after an injury to Malik Davis and the release of Emari Demercado. Before he was injured against the Colts in Week 9, Goodson had racked up 77 yards on 12 carries, and ran for 163 yards on 40 carries for the season. Cowboys May Get Tyler Goodson Back But the good news came down on Thursday amid the wreckage of the past week in Frisco: All is not lost on Goodson. He has sprains to both his PCL and MCL, but assuming the Cowboys stay in the playoff hunt, there is a strong chance we see Goodson again in 2026. According to Patrik Walker of the Cowboys website, there is hope on Goodson. 📰 update: Tyler Goodson suffered a sprained MCL and PCL against the Colts, I’m told. the goal for him, right now, is to return this season — the bye week (+rehab progress) plays a part in that discussion.he’s moving around better every day. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/5EKUkbHhV5 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) November 19, 2026 He wrote: “Update: Tyler Goodson suffered a sprained MCL and PCL against the Colts, I’m told. the goal for him, right now, is to return this season — the bye week (+rehab progress) plays a part in that discussion. “he’s moving around better every day.” Dallas does not have a bye week until Week 14, the week of December 14. The Cowboys have three more games before then and the hope is that the team will know more about his potential return at that point. Losing Goodson was certainly a blow for the Cowboys offense. Coach Brian Schottenheimer was a big booster of his before he went down with the knee injury. He said of Goodson: “I think at the end of the day when you look at we’re rebuilding the room a little bit, the injury to Malik was something that we hated to see happen. Tyler was a guy that we had some love for at the cutdown spot. And we love the veteran presence that he brings, but also the change of pace and the special teams value.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys Could See Return of Injured Breakout Playmaker appeared first on HEAVY .

top.title: Real Madrid have decided to bring back Como star next summer – report
top.description: Real Madrid have decided to bring back Como star next summer – report If Nico Paz’s numbers last season were not impressive enough, the Real Madrid academy graduate has taken his performances to a whole new level this season — both for club and country. Under Cesc Fabregas’ leadership, the team reached this season’s UEFA Champions League with a stunning domestic display last season. So far in the competition, they have looked like one of the finest teams, and Paz has been one of Como’s standouts. In the national team, meanwhile, the player is enjoying a strong run after Lionel Messi’s retirement opened up a spot for him. His performances, needless to say, have got Real Madrid seriously considering a move for him next summer. Decision made One of the pillars of Como’s project. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) As revealed earlier this week, Real Madrid were deeply pondering and internally discussing Paz’s return to the club. Now, as confirmed by COPE , Real Madrid have made their decision: They will bring Paz back to the club next summer. Los Blancos have a buyback clause on the youngster that can only be triggered in the next summer window, after which the club will lose full control of his future. The clause stands at a sum of close to €80 million, and all signs thus point to Real Madrid shelling out that amount for the youngster’s services. Paz’s condition A gem in the making. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) Last summer, everyone expected the Argentine star to return to Madrid after his impressive displays at Como. Paz, however, remain averse to the move as he prioritised playing time over an uncertain role at Real Madrid. One year down the line, the youngster’s condition remains the same, and he will accept the Real Madrid move only if the club can guarantee him a playing role in the team. As of today, it appears complicated for Real Madrid to find a way to accompany Paz alongside Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham, both of whom are starters. If they have made their decision to sign the player, however, they have likely accepted his condition. In that case, it remains to be seen if his arrival causes any cascade in the existing pecking order. In any case, it will be a good problem for the manager to have.

top.title: Tottenham winger explains why Barcelona superstar is different from other footballers: ‘When he plays, you want to watch’
top.description: Tottenham winger explains why Barcelona superstar is different from other footballers: ‘When he plays, you want to watch’ Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhailo Mudryk has singled out Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal as the most entertaining footballer in the world, praising the teenager’s ability to bring creativity, unpredictability and beauty back to the game. Speaking during an interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmytro Gordon , the 25-year-old described Yamal as a player who makes fans want to watch football because of his capacity to produce something extraordinary. The Ukrainian particularly appreciates the unconventional nature of Yamal’s game, believing that his style represents something increasingly rare in modern football. Mudryk explains why Lamine Yamal stands out When asked to identify the most entertaining player in world football, Mudryk did not hesitate to name the Barcelona youngster. Mykhailo Mudryk has praised Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) “The most entertaining player in the world right now? I think it’s Lamine Yamal. He brings back the beauty of football that many fans have forgotten. “When he plays, you want to watch the match because you know he’s going to do something extraordinary and different from the usual,” the Tottenham winger explained. Tottenham forward chooses Messi over Ronaldo in greatest player debate Mudryk also discussed the debate surrounding football’s greatest player, offering an interesting difference between his personal admiration and his assessment of the game’s history. Mykhailo Mudryk feels Lamine Yamal is the most influential player in the sport. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) On one hand, the Ukrainian considers Barcelona legend Lionel Messi the best footballer of all time from an objective standpoint; he admitted that Cristiano Ronaldo has always appealed to him more because of the Portuguese forward’s playing style, mentality and approach to his profession. Mudryk’s praise for the Barcelona talent comes as Lamine continue to defy everything in the sport. At just 19 years of age, the Spaniard is producing numbers that are becoming hard to replicate not only for players his age, but also for those who have been in the sport for a very long time.

nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. nigeria.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
nigeria.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. nigeria.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
nigeria.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. nigeria.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. nigeria.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
nigeria.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. Having also suffered neurological absence seizures during pre-season in August, Musiala has managed just four appearances so far in the 2026-27 campaign. Kompany, however, backed his star to emerge stronger from the ordeal, pointing to Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane as proof of what players can achieve in Munich. "When players like him go through a difficult spell, they can draw strength from it - both mentally and physically," Kompany stated. "When I arrived, he was a 'golden child'. Seeing how he's handling the whole situation now is something special. I hope that in six months' time, it'll be a completely different story." Positive updates on Luis Diaz and Alphonso Davies Alongside Musiala's impending comeback, Kompany delivered encouraging fitness bulletins regarding wingers Luis Diaz and full-back Alphonso Davies. While Friday's visit from Koln comes slightly too soon for Diaz, the Colombian international is nearing full availability. "Lucho is doing very well. He's had a good week. Tomorrow's still a bit too soon for him, but we'll be able to get him back in action within the next seven days," Kompany revealed, before adding a brief reassurance on Davies: "Phonzy will be fine; I can't say any more than that at the moment." Reinforcements arrive for crucial winter run Getting key stars back on the grass provides a timely boost for Kompany, who has also just returned from his own four-week medical absence. With Bayern sitting atop the Bundesliga as the only unbeaten team across Europe's top five leagues, Musiala's creativity will prove vital across eight fixtures before the winter break.

sports.title: 'It was certainly a shock' - Vincent Kompany reveals honest truth behind four-week Bayern Munich absence
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-BAYERN MUNICH-ARSENAL - AFP Vincent Kompany is officially back on the touchline for Bayern Munich ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln. After spending four weeks away recovering from a health scare, the Belgian coach has opened up on his medical tests, rival managers' support, and watching his side from home. Kompany returns to the Allianz Arena dugout Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is back on the touchline ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln at the Allianz Arena. Having missed four weeks following a health scare caused by meningeal irritation, the 40-year-old welcomed his international players back to Sabener Strasse on Thursday after receiving full medical clearance . "I'm very grateful for the support I've received from the club and the doctors. I'm feeling really well again now and am delighted to be back with the team," Kompany said. "All the tests came back positive. I have to say, I'm in very good health; we've done lots of tests, all of which have come back clear." Admitting he ignored warning signs Kompany admitted his enforced break served as a wake-up call after he initially failed to listen to his body following an earlier Champions League tie against Arsenal. Despite the initial alarm, he thanked rival managers and his family for standing by him during his recovery. "I don't want to play it down; it was certainly a shock. But it was a result of me carrying on when I really should have taken a break," Kompany explained. "As well as my family, I'd also like to thank the coaching community. We're always competing against one another, but almost every coach has got in touch with me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps even had our differences." Praising his backroom staff from afar During his time away, Kompany stepped back completely from matchday decisions, trusting assistants Rene Maric, Aaron Danks, Floribert Ngalula and Daniel Fradley to maintain standards. Watching from home, he highlighted Bayern's fearless Champions League display against Atletico Madrid as a standout memory. "I didn't make any decisions," he noted. "When the head coach is absent, the handover has to be such that things carry on as they always do. They managed that very well. I really enjoyed the Atletico match. It was one of the finest moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn't there." Motivated for the pre-Christmas sprint Refreshed and armed with fresh tactical ideas gathered during his time off, Kompany is eager to lead Europe's last remaining unbeaten side in the top five leagues into a gruelling run of eight matches in 29 days. "There's one person at FC Bayern who is really motivated for this game against Koln. I've been waiting for four weeks," Kompany concluded. "If the players can sense my motivation, we'll have a good foundation for tomorrow's match."

sports.title: Ducks "flat as a pancake" in shutout loss in Colorado
sports.description: Nov 19, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Colorado Avalanche center Brock Nelson (11) celebrates after his goal in the second period against the Anaheim Ducks at Ball Arena. DENVER – Joel Quenneville provided the most aptly succinct description of the Anaheim Ducks first shutout loss of the season. “We were flat as a pancake,” the Ducks coach said. Anaheim’s chronic defensive issues persisted following a competitive opening period, and the Ducks previously scalding hot offense was completely snowed under by the Colorado Avalanche in a sound defeat, 4-0, on Thursday at Ball Arena. Anaheim (11-11-1, 23 points) has lost four of its last five games following a five-game winning streak and has allowed four or more goals in 14 of its 23 games. “I think everything (was disconnected),” Jackson LaCombe said. “We turned too many pucks over. Just didn't have any jam on the offense. Throwing pucks away early. Didn't have any possession time. There’s things we’ve gotta fix.” Cutter Gauthier’s historically prolific 10-game goal streak came to a halt. Gauthier recorded just two shots and only one on the power play, as the Avalanche penalty kill rightly shaded his one-timer spot. Teemu Selanne maintains his hold on the longest goal streak in franchise history (11 games, 1997-98). All of Anaheim’s top performers were stagnant against Colorado, with Gauthier, Leo Carlsson, Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund combining for three total shots. The Ducks spent an inordinate amount of time in their own defensive zone, as they again turned the puck over on their half of the ice, struggled on clears and couldn’t connect on clean breakouts. Stian Solberg, 2024 first-round pick, made his NHL debut, and with the 20-year-old Norwegian defenseman cracking the line-up, Anaheim iced a blue line with an average age of 22.67 years old. “Tough loss, but most fun game I ever played,” Solberg said. “It's cool to be out there on the biggest stage in the world. It's just something we've been kind of just looking at your whole life and when it finally happens, it's very special.” Nicolas Roy opened the scoring after an all-around failure by Anaheim on the opening draw of the second period. Beckett Sennecke couldn’t control the puck, fell at his own blue line, and the Avalanche pounced to send Roy walking around Lukáš Dostál, 1-0, eight seconds into the middle frame. Momentum continued to slide Colorado’s way, as Brock Nelson blasted a power-play one-timer three minutes later, 2-0. The Avalanche had the first three power plays of the night. Nelson netted another just under seven minutes later, as he toe-dragged around Jackson LaCombe and picked top glove on Dostál, 3-0. Another turnover ended up in the back of the Ducks net, as Devon Toews finished in the slot, 4-0, with just under 10 minutes to play. technology.title: Support tech fixed malware by charging client less for their services
technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. It’s still on his desk!" Have you done less tech support to deliver more value? If so, click here to send On Call an email and charge us with the responsibility of telling your story on a future Friday. ®

technology.title: Big Tech's compliance with EU market rules is performative, consumer group says
technology.description: Big Tech has earned a finger-wagging from the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), which says the industry's compliance with the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) still leaves consumers short of meaningful choice. BEUC said : "Big Tech companies Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft (so-called 'gatekeepers') still likely breach the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) far too often for consumers to reap the full benefits of real choice over their digital services and products." The European Commission designated the six companies as gatekeepers in 2023 , imposing obligations on specified core platform services such as search engines, messaging services, and app stores. The DMA aims to make digital markets fairer and more open to competition. The devil is in the details. In the years since, the EC has lined up Amazon and Microsoft's cloud businesses for gatekeeper status. In March 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings against Alphabet over Search and Google Play, while separately specifying measures Apple had to take to meet its interoperability obligations. In 2024, Microsoft's browser rivals argued that Edge should also be covered by the DMA's gatekeeper obligations, and so on. BEUC is a fan of the act – it published a report on its consumer benefits in 2025 – but is less impressed with industry's implementation. Its latest analysis draws together evidence of potential breaches submitted to the Commission between June 2025 and June 2026. In the case of Microsoft, BEUC stated that the company used "behavioural techniques" and "non-neutral interfaces" to elicit consent from users for data sharing across services – emphasizing benefits, while not explaining why a user might want to decline. The Windows behemoth is also accused of making it tricky to change defaults and stop behavior such as apps opening links in Edge or using Bing as a search engine. "Microsoft also regularly prompts users who have selected an alternative browser or search engine to switch to Edge or Bing using increasingly subliminal techniques, such as prompts coming from the device manufacturer, which undermine effective compliance with the DMA," BEUC said. Then there's Google, which was fined €890 million in July for favoring its own services in Search and restricting developers' ability to direct Play Store users to alternative purchasing channels. As with Microsoft, BEUC expressed concerns about the non-neutral language Google used to obtain user consent, as well as how it allegedly made it difficult to change default settings or uninstall gatekeeper applications. The alleged behavior of Apple, ByteDance, Amazon, and Meta was also highlighted, with examples including Apple's restrictions on alternative app distribution and Amazon using interface design techniques to nudge users into handing over their data. technology.description: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) allowed Nvidia and AMD to sell hundreds of thousands of advanced GPUs to entities that the Department of War classifies as “Chinese military companies” that help Beijing to build its military. That news comes courtesy of Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, who asked BIS to provide information about NVIDIA’s and AMD’s applications for the export licenses required to sell advanced AI chips to China. The congressman on Thursday revealed requests to sell 3.4 million AI chips to China, and that BIS approved the sale of 879,000 items. BIS refused to authorize some giant deals for Nvidia, which applied to sell 610,000 chips to Alibaba and 508,000 to TikTok owner Bytedance. But the agency allowed many other sales, including to Alibaba and Tencent. Mast points out that both of those companies are on the Department of War’s List of Chinese Military Companies , the designation it uses for entities deemed to be a “military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base.” That’s a polite way of saying that Washington thinks China relies on these companies to operate and improve its military, and therefore to challenge America’s national security. Advanced chips are essential when designing nuclear weapons, stealthy submarines, or advanced aircraft. Those applications are the core reason the US bans exports of advanced GPUs to China, so that the People’s Liberation Army can’t develop advanced weapons. A diverting drama The congressman also claims that some of Nvidia’s applications were attempts to sell its wares to “chip-smuggling fronts to facilitate their sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies.” The New York Times reports that some of those front entities are linked to Megaspeed, the outfit fronted by suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang, whose intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a key factor in his resignation. Megaspeed is accused of what the US calls “diversion” – claiming to buy chips for one reason while intending to either ship them to China or rent them exclusively to Chinese companies in ways that breach the spirit of export restrictions if not the letter of the law. One of the documents Mast shared says “Every Nvidia and AMD application stated that the proposed transfer posed a ‘low’ risk of diversion.” Mast’s point therefore appears to be that the BIS has authorized sales that go against the clear intent of established policy, and the national interest, and that Nvidia and AMD may have been a little too optimistic in their assessment of diversion risk. technology.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMware also wants its users to address CVE-2026-123891, which allows attackers to read and write the database used by SDDC Manager, the tool for managing entire software-defined datacenters. Attackers can execute arbitrary commands and elevate privileges to root. The prospect of an unknown party getting access to vCenter or SDDC manager is not pleasant. At least VMware has fixed its software. The virty giant hasn't done the same to address a second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , which warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). VMware plans to ship new versions of its products with a patched version of Apache, but for now only has workarounds that disable the http2 protocol. A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. technology.description: The Germ Network encrypted messaging client, known as Germ DM, became available for Android on Wednesday, and made a bigger splash than its iOS touchdown back in 2023. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. And our vision for the product that will continue shipping over the coming years is that these cards become a more intelligent way to manage your social life, even your work life." At some point, AI might play a role in that, but both Xue and Brown expressed reservations about the current state of play. Citing concerns Signal has raised about the integration of AI and messaging, Xue said, "The products today that I might characterize as technology demos, they're most powerful when they run on someone else's computer. So you end up with these systems where you upload all your messages or you give another entity the power to observe your computing, and that's extremely dangerous for what we protect as private content." Xue noted rapid progress toward addressing information exposure concerns and therefore plans to explore the kinds of smart tooling that users want while also meeting security and privacy requirements. science.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
science.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

science.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Stormy Southwest Pacific Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa.
